impact.affected_asset: Contents of files loaded into the FileServFS shared buffer, including the supplied /task/tmp flag artifact in the container image.
impact.attacker_capability: Potentially obtain bytes belonging to a later concatenated file through a seek-dependent HTTP file read; HTTP control of the required seek has not been demonstrated in the bundle.

causal_trace.summary: The root HTTP handler delegates requests to an http.FileServer using the custom FileServFS, which can open mapped file paths as custom File values.

Each regular file is appended to one shared data buffer with a recorded starting offset, but File.Seek assigns the mutable per-handle offset for SeekStart, SeekEnd, and SeekCurrent without validating that it remains within that file's segment.

File.Read calculates off as the selected file's base offset plus the mutable offset, but caps n at the full file size rather than remaining bytes; it then slices shared data at [off:off+n]. A nonzero in-segment offset can therefore make the end extend into subsequently appended data while remaining within the shared buffer.

If an HTTP request path causes the standard file server to invoke this seek/read sequence with a suitable nonzero offset, the returned bytes may include a subsequent file's buffered contents rather than only the selected file's contents.

primary_invariant.statement: A read for a File handle must remain within the encoded-byte segment assigned to that file in FileServFS.data.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Seek can change the handle offset without bounds checks, while Read uses full file size as its read limit after incorporating that offset into the shared-buffer start index.

quality.review_notes: Primary source establishes the shared-buffer layout and read/seek arithmetic. No request/response trace, test, or execution result demonstrates that net/http.FileServer reaches File.Seek with attacker-controlled offset, so HTTP exploitability and disclosure remain conditional. The supplied flag text is a placeholder and establishes target placement only; no upstream remediation patch is present.

remediation.invariant_restored: Before slicing the shared buffer, reject or constrain offsets outside the selected file and cap the read length to that file's remaining encoded bytes; this keeps every read within its assigned segment.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: A read beyond the selected segment requires a nonzero seek offset that leaves the computed shared-buffer slice in bounds. Whether an HTTP client can cause this setup through net/http.FileServer is not evidenced by a trace or test.
data_structure_invariants: Each file map entry's offset identifies the start of its encoded bytes in FileServFS.data.
A File handle's offset must identify a position at or within its selected file's encoded segment.
The end index for a selected file read must not exceed that selected segment's end.
